# FL Studio Agent

Drive FL Studio from an AI agent: an MCP server that writes notes, sets tempo, levels and plugin parameters, checks which channels sound, and renders the mix, in your own FL Studio.
Source, docs, and the native Bridge plugin: https://github.com/origami-research/fl-studio-agent

## Quick start

You need FL Studio 2026 on macOS or Windows and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).

1. **Install uv** if you don't have it.
   macOS: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`.
   Windows: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"`, then install [loopMIDI](https://www.tobias-erichsen.de/software/loopmidi.html) and add two ports named exactly `FLMCP Req` and `FLMCP Res` (Windows has no virtual MIDI ports; macOS needs nothing).
2. **Set up FL Studio once.** Start FL once if you never have, close it, then run:

   ```bash
   uvx --python 3.12 --from fl-studio-agent fl-mcp-install
   ```

   It installs the controller and note scripts, assigns the controller's MIDI ports, and creates the agent's own project (`FLMCP Agent.flp`; your other projects are never touched).
   It is safe to rerun.
   To update later, run it with `fl-studio-agent@latest` in place of `fl-studio-agent` and restart FL and your client.
3. **Add the server to your client** with a button above or a config below, open FL Studio, and ask for "a 4-bar chord loop in A minor".

Live writes and `render` also need the native [Bridge plugin](https://github.com/origami-research/fl-studio-agent/blob/main/SETUP.md#the-bridge-plugin), built once from source; without it notes still land, with FL reloading the project per write.

Download [fl-studio-agent.mcpb](https://github.com/origami-research/fl-studio-agent/releases/latest/download/fl-studio-agent.mcpb) and open it (or drag it into Settings > Extensions).

Or add this to `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings > Developer > Edit Config):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fl-studio": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--python",
        "3.12",
        "fl-studio-agent"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

If Claude Desktop reports `spawn uvx ENOENT`, it cannot see your shell's PATH: replace `"uvx"` with the full path that `which uvx` (macOS) or `where uvx` (Windows) prints.
</details>

## Troubleshooting

Run the doctor while FL Studio is open:

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 --from fl-studio-agent fl-mcp-doctor
```

It prints one JSON report of the control plane (controller script and MIDI ports), the note plane, and the agent project, with a `fix` for anything not connected.
The usual fixes: open FL Studio before your client starts the server; after an upgrade rerun step 2 with `fl-studio-agent@latest` (a stale controller is reported); on Windows, keep loopMIDI running with both ports.
Using the FL Studio trial? Set `FLMCP_FL_LICENSE=trial` in the server's `env`, because the trial cannot reopen saved projects.
`uvx --python 3.12 fl-studio-agent --version` prints the installed version.
<!-- install:end -->

## Tools

`run` (Python against the FL SDK; its docstring is the SDK cheatsheet), `get_scene` (what FL has now), `check` (play a few bars and read which channels sounded), `render` (record the mix to WAV), and `analyze` (WAV analysis).
The full description is in the [repository README](https://github.com/origami-research/fl-studio-agent#tools).
